cohort: The cohort consisted of 90 pregnant women diagnosed with Gestational Diabetes Mellitus (GDM) in a tertiary care hospital.
finding: The study found a GDM prevalence of 16.7%, with obesity, family history of diabetes, and previous GDM identified as primary risk factors, leading to obstetric outcomes such as preterm births (10%), macrosomia (6.7%), and cesarean deliveries (13.3%).
mod_finding: Cesarean deliveries occurred in 13.3% of the GDM cohort.
